title: Set 262

sentences.ko: 모르겠어. 그냥 그 일 받을까 계속 생각하는데, 상사한테 말하는 장면을 떠올리면 속이 좀 울렁거려. 잠깐 다른 얘기 하면 안 될까? 나중에 생각해 볼게.
sentences.text: I don't know, I keep thinking I should just take the job, but then I picture telling my boss and I kind of feel sick. Can we talk about something else for a bit? I'll figure it out later.

alts.text: Ugh, part of me's like, just take the job already, but then I imagine telling my boss and I kinda wanna throw up. Can we change the subject for a bit? I'll deal with it later.

I am not certain. I keep thinking that I should simply accept the position, but when I imagine telling my manager, I feel quite unwell. Would it be possible to discuss something else for a while? I will work it out later.

sentences.note: **take the job** 은 제안받은 일자리를 받아들인다는 뜻이에요. **I'll figure it out later** 는 지금은 미뤄 두고 나중에 답을 찾겠다는 말이에요.
sentences.situation: 친구한테 고민 상담하면서 결론은 못 내리기

sentences.ko: 오늘 회의에서 우리 팀장이 내 아이디어를 가져가서 자기 것처럼 발표했거든. 끝나고 내가 그 얘기를 꺼냈더니 우리는 다 한 팀이래. 아니, 그럼 슬라이드에는 왜 자기 이름이 있는 건데?
sentences.text: So my manager took my idea in the meeting today and presented it like it was his, and when I brought it up after, he said we're all one team. Like, okay, then why is your name on the slide?

alts.text: My manager straight up stole my idea in the meeting today, acted like it was his, and when I said something after, he goes, we're all one team. Okay, so why's your name on the slide?

In today's meeting, my manager presented my idea as though it were his own, and when I raised the matter afterward, he said that we are all one team. If that is the case, why is his name on the slide?

sentences.note: **brought it up** 은 어떤 이야기를 꺼냈다는 뜻이에요. 캐주얼한 쪽의 **straight up** 은 대놓고, 아예 라는 느낌을 더해 줘요.
sentences.situation: 회사 사람 때문에 짜증난 걸 친구한테 털어놓기

sentences.ko: 요즘 열한 시쯤 눕는데, 생각이 안 멈춰서 결국 누운 채로 회사에서 했던 말들을 곱씹게 돼. 그러다 겨우 잠들 만하면 일어날 시간이야.
sentences.text: I've been going to bed at like eleven, but my brain just won't shut off, so I end up lying there going over stuff I said at work. And then right when I finally fall asleep, it's time to get up.

alts.text: I'm getting in bed around eleven, but my brain won't turn off, so I'm just lying there replaying stuff I said at work. Then the second I finally doze off, boom, alarm's going off.
I have been going to bed at around eleven, but my mind will not settle, so I end up lying awake reviewing things I said at work. Then, just as I finally fall asleep, it is time to get up.

sentences.note: **won't shut off** 는 생각이 멈추지 않는다는 뜻으로, 머리가 꺼지지 않는다는 느낌이에요. **end up** 은 결국 ~하게 되다 라는 뜻이에요.

sentences.ko: 음, 걔가 편해지면 진짜 웃긴데 처음엔 좀 조용해. 그러니까 처음 십 분 동안 말이 별로 없어도 서운해하지 마. 그리고 걔 요리도 해, 흉내만 내는 게 아니라 진짜로. 그래서 너희 둘이 잘 맞을 것 같아.
sentences.text: Okay, so he's really funny once he gets comfortable, but he's kind of quiet at first, so don't take it personally if he doesn't say much for the first ten minutes. And he cooks, like actually cooks, so I think you two would get along.

alts.text: He's super funny once he warms up, but he's kinda quiet at first, so don't read into it if he barely talks the first ten minutes. Oh, and he really cooks, like for real, so I think you guys'd hit it off.

He is very funny once he feels comfortable, but he is rather quiet at first, so please do not take it personally if he says little for the first ten minutes. He also genuinely cooks, so I believe the two of you would get along well.

sentences.note: **don't take it personally** 는 너 때문이 아니니까 서운해하지 마 라는 뜻이에요. **get along** 은 사이좋게 잘 지내다, 캐주얼한 쪽의 **hit it off** 는 처음 만나자마자 죽이 잘 맞다 라는 뜻이에요.
sentences.situation: 친구 소개팅 주선하면서 상대가 어떤 사람인지 설명하기

sentences.ko: 헬스장 가려던 참에 언니한테 전화가 와서, 끊고 나니까 거의 아홉 시였어. 그래도 갈 수는 있었는데, 그렇게 늦게 운동하면 밤새 잠 못 잘 걸 알아서 그냥 저녁 해 먹었어.
sentences.text: I was about to leave for the gym, but then my sister called, and by the time we hung up it was almost nine. I could've still gone, but I knew I'd be up all night if I worked out that late, so I just made dinner instead.

alts.text: I was just heading out to the gym when my sister called, and by the time we got off the phone it was almost nine. Coulda still gone, but I'd never sleep if I worked out that late, so I made dinner instead.

I was about to leave for the gym when my sister called, and by the time our conversation ended it was nearly nine. I could still have gone, but I knew I would be awake all night if I exercised so late, so I prepared dinner instead.

sentences.note: **I was about to** 는 막 ~하려던 참이었다 라는 뜻이에요. **by the time** 은 ~할 즈음에는, ~했을 때는 이미 라는 뜻으로 써요.
sentences.situation: 운동 가려다 말게 된 핑계 대기

reviewed: 1번 한국어: '그 자리 가겠다고 할까'는 take the job 뜻이 흐려서 '그 일 받을까'로 고침
3번 한국어: '머리가 도무지 안 꺼져서'는 번역투라 '생각이 안 멈춰서'로 고침
4번 영어: don't take it the wrong way 는 보통 내가 할 말 앞에 붙이는 표현이라, 상대가 말이 없는 것을 서운해하지 말라는 자리에는 don't take it personally 가 맞음. note 도 따라 고침
4번 한국어: '그러니까'가 두 번 나오고 '걔 요리를 해, 진짜 제대로'가 어색해서 다듬음
